records.lessonFeedback:

records.lessonFeedback:

Lại một lần nữa làm rất tốt. Em nói trôi chảy, thân thiện, nội dung chi tiết và phần kết bài đầy ấn tượng. Tuy nhiên, phát âm vẫn là điểm yếu chính cần khắc phục. reviews.title: Nguyễn Ngọc Thuỳ Dương · IELTS 48 · W09 · Đề 1
reviews.scopeMarkdown: **Số từ bài gốc: 214 từ**, đếm trên nguyên văn bằng cách tách theo khoảng trắng; đủ tối thiểu 150 từ nhưng vượt 14 từ so với giới hạn 150–200 từ của lớp. Cô chỉ chấm Đề 1 đã gõ; không chấm Đề 2 hoặc bản scan.
reviews.overall: Cô yêu cầu em sửa và nộp lại. Bài này em làm còn ẩu ở những lỗi câu cụ thể: “These numbers, however, still below…” thiếu động từ chính, còn “Italy… grew” đặt tên nước làm chủ thể tăng. Số liệu Belgium cũng chưa đúng, khiến bài mất quan hệ đồng hạng cuối kỳ. Em đã vận dụng cấu trúc with và after which, nhưng cần dùng kiến thức ấy trong câu hoàn chỉnh, đúng dữ liệu. Overview còn thiếu thông tin thấp nhất và bài vượt giới hạn độ dài. Mục đích đi học là ghi chép, hiểu và vận dụng để tự viết; em đọc lại bài học và tự sửa các câu được đánh dấu.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em đặt Germany, Italy và France trong Detail 1; United Kingdom và Belgium trong Detail 2. Cách chia này hợp lý theo thứ hạng cuối kỳ, nên Cô giữ cả nhóm và thứ tự trình bày. France có đỉnh và đứng đầu năm 2004; em đã chọn được mốc này, cần giữ khi rút bài. Hai nước ở Detail 2 cùng đạt khoảng 28% năm 2012, thấp hơn ba nước đã nêu ở Detail 1.

The given line graph illustrates the share of female representatives in parliaments in five European nations between 2000 and 2012.
   Overall, there was an increase in the proportion of women holding parliamentary seats in all the surveyed, with the UK witnessing the most pronounced rise. Notably, in the last year given, Italy recorded the highest figure.
   To elaborate, in 2000, the percentage of women represented in parliament in Germany stood at approximately 33%, the highest figure on the chart, before remaining relatively stable and rising to just over 35% in 2012. Italy, meanwhile, grew more sharply, from 26% in 2000 to nearly 40% in 2012.  The figure for France, conversely, rose dramatically, going from 25% to 37% in 2004 and before dropping markedly by about 10% in 2008 and then gradually increasing to 32% in the final year.
   Regarding the remaining, both the UK and Belgium experienced considerable growth. Starting at the lowest point of 5% in 2000, the figure for the UK increased significantly to approximately 20% in 2008 before reaching nearly 30% in the final year. Belgium; likewise, saw a notable rise from around 12% to 25% over the first four years, after which the figure remained virtually unchanged until 2012. These numbers, however, still below those of Germany, Italy, and France.

Italy, meanwhile, grew more sharply, from 26% in 2000 to nearly 40% in 2012.  The figure for France, conversely, rose dramatically, going from 25% to 37% in 2004 and before dropping markedly by about 10% in 2008 and then gradually increasing to 32% in the final year.

Regarding the remaining, both the UK and Belgium experienced considerable growth. Starting at the lowest point of 5% in 2000, the figure for the UK increased significantly to approximately 20% in 2008 before reaching nearly 30% in the final year. Belgium; likewise, saw a notable rise from around 12% to 25% over the first four years, after which the figure remained virtually unchanged until 2012. The given pie charts illustrate the main reasons why students chose a particular university in the UK between 1997 and 2007.
   Overall, the proportion of students choosing a university for its suitable degree courses was the highest in both years, while the figure for proximity to the parental home increased the most. In contrast, good sports and social activities experienced the most significant decline, becoming the least popular factor in 2007.
   To elaborate, suitable degree courses accounted for the highest proportion in 1997, at 35%, before rising slightly to 37% in 2007. The figure for proximity to the parental home, meanwhile, increased more sharply, more than doubling from 10% to 22% over the ten-year period. Similarly, the percentage of students choosing a university because of the quality of teaching rose moderately from 15% to 18%.
   Regarding the remaining factors, both experienced declines. Starting at 21% in 1997, the figure for the quality of resources fell slightly to 17% in 2007. Good sports and social activities,conversely, saw the biggest fall, decreasing from 19% to just 6% in the final year.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given bar chart illustrates the annual pay, in thousands of US dollars, for doctors and other workers in seven countries in 2004.

Overall, doctors earned considerably more than other workers in all seven countries. The US recorded the highest figure for doctors, while Finland had the lowest. Also of note is that Switzerland and France had the same level of pay for doctors, whereas the figure for other workers was highest in the US.

To elaborate, doctors in the US earned an impressive 120 thousand US dollars, marking the highest point in the chart. This was followed by Switzerland and France, with both figures standing at around 70 thousand dollars. The respective figures for doctors in the Czech Republic and Germany were approximately 64 and 63 thousand dollars, while Italy recorded around 60 thousand dollars. Finland had the lowest figure, at only 50 thousand dollars.

Regarding other workers, the US also recorded the highest figure, at around 46 thousand dollars, followed by Switzerland at 40 thousand. France had a figure of approximately 29 thousand dollars, while Finland recorded around 26 thousand. The figures for Italy, the Czech Republic and Germany were the same, at about 20 thousand dollars each. These numbers, however, were considerably lower than those for doctors in every country.
